title: Who can apply (ukri.org)
text:
Who is eligible to apply
This opportunity is open to organisations with standard eligibility and to mayoral strategic, local or combined or regional authorities who apply under non-standard eligibility .
Check if your organisation is eligible .
Project leads and co-leads from mayoral strategic, local or combined or regional authorities may need to go through additional funding assurance checks before being awarded funding .
The lead organisation will be responsible for submitting the grant application.
Project lead
The project lead for this funding opportunity can be based at a UK research organisation eligible for UKRI funding or from the mayoral strategic,local or combined or regional authorities.
To apply, you must be based at an eligible organisation as follows:
higher education providers
research institutes
public sector research establishments
NHS bodies
independent research organisations. Check if your organisation is eligible
a Mayoral Strategic Authority, or other local government partner that has been granted non-standard eligibility for this funding opportunity
Mayoral strategic, local or combined or regional authorities and other local government partners that are not currently at UKRI-eligible organisations can apply for ‘non-standard’ eligibility limited to the Local Opportunity Lab and should contact opportunitymission@ukri.org to discuss their eligibility application.
We may ask for organisations applying under the ‘non-standard’ route to undertake eligibility checks before your application is submitted via The UKRI Funding Service to ensure any potential delays are minimised.
Business, third sector and international organisations are not eligible to apply as the project lead on behalf of the local opportunity lab.
The project lead must ensure that they contribute an appropriate proportion of their time to the overall leadership and coordination of the grant, in addition to any time allocated to research and knowledge mobilisation activities.
Applications may be submitted jointly by more than one applicant. In such cases, one person must be regarded as the project lead taking the lead responsibility for the conduct of the project and the observance of the terms and conditions.
Correspondence regarding the application and grant will be addressed to the project lead only (and in the case of any offer letter, to their office).
Project co-lead
Applications must include at least one project co-lead from their relevant mayoral strategic, local or combined or regional authorities, UK-based educational providers, research organisations, and business, third and private sectors subject to ESRC eligibility and costing rules .
As an exception for this funding opportunity, you may allocate more than the usual 30% of total costs (at 100% FEC) to non-academic partners where clearly justified. The combined time commitment of staff from non-academic partners can also exceed one year FTE for the duration of the project. The combined costs of any project co-leads from UK business, third sector or government organisations on an application cannot be more than 70% of the total FEC.
This flexibility will enable the meaningful involvement of key local and regional stakeholders, whose participation is critical to effective operation and capacity to deliver impact.
If you wish to exceed the 30% cost threshold or the combined time commitment cap, you must clearly justify this in your proposal, specifically within the ‘Resources and costs’ section.
For this funding opportunity, project co-leads from government organisations can also claim staff salary costs as long as their role is being backfilled. These salary costs will need to adhere to the Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) project co-leads from the ESRC project co-leads from UK business, third sector or government organisations policy and be fully justified, and the backfill commitment evidenced.
Eligible costs remain the same as those outlined in the ESRC project co-leads from UK business, third sector or government organisations policy .
While certain eligible costs may be funded at 100% FEC, in line with UKRI policy , this does not increase the overall funding available.
We also strongly encourage you to explain your planned approach and its rationale when answering the application questions on ‘Applicant and team capability to deliver’ and ‘Public Partnerships’.
Who is not eligible to apply
Non-UK organisations and UK partners not based at approved organisations are not eligible to apply as project leads or co-leads.
International researchers
International researchers can apply as project partners. You should include all other international collaborators (or UK partners not based at approved organisations) as project partners.
Please consider UKRI guidance on Roles in funding applications: eligibility, responsibilities and costings guidance .
Resubmissions
We will not accept uninvited resubmissions of projects that have been submitted to UKRI. Find out more about UKRI’s resubmission policy .
Equality, diversity and inclusion
We are committed to achieving equality of opportunity for all funding applicants. We encourage applications from a diverse range of researchers.
We support people to work in a way that suits their personal circumstances. This includes:
career breaks
support for people with caring responsibilities
flexible working
alternative working patterns
UKRI can offer disability and accessibility support for UKRI applicants and grant holders during the application and assessment process.
